de-payroll-benefits.before: **The EUR 50 limit.** Benefits valued at market price under § 8(2) sentence 1 EStG stay out of pay if the total net benefit in the month is not over EUR 50. It is a cliff: at EUR 50.01 the whole amount is taxable. Benefits valued by a special rule (company car, official meal values, staff discounts under § 8(3)) do not count toward it and cannot use it. Vouchers and cash cards that only buy goods or services and meet the payment-services criteria count as benefits in kind, but only if given on top of the pay already owed (§ 8(1) sentence 3 and § 8(2) sentence 11 EStG). "On top of pay owed" means no offset against pay, no pay cut in exchange, not instead of an agreed raise, and no pay rise if the benefit stops (§ 8(4) EStG). The same EUR 50 limit applies for contributions (§ 3(1) SvEV).
de-payroll-benefits.after:
**The EUR 50 limit.** Benefits valued at market price under § 8(2) sentence 1 EStG stay out of pay if the total net benefit in the month is not over EUR 50. It is a cliff: at EUR 50.01 the whole amount is taxable. Benefits valued by a special rule (company car, official meal values, staff discounts under § 8(3)) do not count toward it and cannot use it. Vouchers and cash cards that only buy goods or services and meet the payment-services criteria count as benefits in kind, but only if given on top of the pay already owed (§ 8(1) sentence 3 and § 8(2) sentence 11 EStG). "On top of pay owed" means no offset against pay, no pay cut in exchange, not instead of an agreed raise, and no pay rise if the benefit stops (§ 8(4) EStG). The same EUR 50 limit applies for contributions (§ 3(1) SvEV).

**Qualifying staff discounts.** Under § 8(3), use the end price offered to unrelated final consumers in ordinary commerce by the employer or the customer nearest the place of supply, reduced by 4%. The goods/services must not be predominantly produced, distributed or provided for employees and must not be taxed under § 40. Subtract the employee's payment, then the unused part of the EUR 1,080 annual allowance for benefits from that employment: taxable benefit = max(0, 96% of that applicable public end price − employee payment − remaining annual allowance). Track annual aggregation; do not also use the monthly EUR 50 cliff. At public price EUR 2,000/payment EUR 500, benefit before allowance is EUR 1,420; with the full annual allowance remaining, taxable benefit is EUR 340.

de-payroll-benefits.before: **Meals and lodging.** Meals and lodging use the SvEV values for both tax and contributions (§ 8(2) sentences 6 and 7 EStG). For 2026: EUR 345 a month for full board, EUR 2.37 per breakfast and EUR 4.57 per lunch or dinner, EUR 285 a month for lodging (§ 2 SvEV). The taxable amount is the official value less what the employee pays. Canteen meals, and meals on business trips valued at the official value, can be taxed at a 25% flat rate (§ 40(2) sentence 1 nos. 1 and 1a EStG). A trip meal costing up to EUR 60 is not taxed at all where the employee could claim the travel meal allowance (§ 8(2) sentences 8 and 9 EStG). Travel meal allowances paid above the tax-free flat rates can be taxed at 25% up to the same amount again (§ 40(2) sentence 1 no. 4 EStG).
de-payroll-benefits.after: **Meals and lodging.** Meals and lodging use the SvEV values for both tax and contributions (§ 8(2) sentences 6 and 7 EStG). For 2026: EUR 345 a month for full board, EUR 2.37 per breakfast and EUR 4.57 per lunch or dinner, EUR 285 a month for lodging (§ 2 SvEV). The taxable amount is the official value less what the employee pays. Canteen meals, and meals on business trips valued at the official value, can be taxed at a 25% flat rate (§ 40(2) sentence 1 nos. 1 and 1a EStG). A trip meal costing up to EUR 60 is not taxed at all where the employee could claim the travel meal allowance (§ 8(2) sentences 8 and 9 EStG). Travel meal allowances paid above the tax-free flat rates can be taxed at 25% up to the same amount again (§ 40(2) sentence 1 no. 4 EStG). Lodging is distinct from a dwelling. Apply each relevant § 2(3) reduction to the EUR 285 lodging value: 15% for admission to the employer's household or community lodging; 15% for under-18s or apprentices; and 40% for two employees sharing, 50% for three, or 60% for more than three. Two otherwise ordinary adult occupants give EUR 171 each for a full month before payments. Where the ordinary lodging value is inequitable in the actual case, use the statutory local-rent alternative. A dwelling normally uses local rent, taking account of impairment from its location relative to the business and applicable statutory rent limits, with § 8(2) sentence 12 EStG applied correspondingly. Only if local rent is extraordinarily difficult to establish may the statutory EUR 5.01/m² monthly proxy apply, or EUR 4.10/m² for basic equipment without central heating or without a bath/shower. Value energy, water and other ancillary costs at the usual local price. For shorter periods use 1/30 per day, applying the relevant percentage reductions to the daily value; perform calculations at two decimal places, rounding up where the third digit is 5–9 (§ 2(3)–(6) SvEV).

de-payroll-benefits.before: - **§ 37b, 30%.** The employer may pay 30% income tax on all non-cash benefits granted in a business year on top of pay owed (to employees) or on top of the agreed service (to customers and business partners). The base is the employer's cost including VAT. Costs per recipient a year count only up to EUR 10,000; the excess is taxed normally. A single gift costing more than EUR 10,000 is excluded in full (§ 37b(1) sentence 3 EStG; BMF letter of 19 May 2015, Rn. 21). It does not apply to company cars, official meal values, staff discounts, items under § 40(2) or shares (§ 37b(2) sentence 2). The choice is made once for the business year, but separately for third parties and for own employees; for own employees the calendar year counts (BMF letter of 19 May 2015, BStBl I p. 468, Rn. 4). Items costing up to EUR 10 are treated as promotional giveaways and can be left out (same letter). The recipient is told the tax was paid and leaves the item out of income (§ 37b(3) EStG). For own employees the item stays subject to contributions: only gifts to third parties' employees are excluded from pay for social insurance (§ 1(1) no. 14 SvEV).
de-payroll-benefits.after: - **§ 37b, 30%.** The employer may pay 30% income tax on all non-cash benefits granted in a business year on top of pay owed (to employees) or on top of the agreed service (to customers and business partners). The base is the giver's cost including VAT; for employees of affiliated companies, it is at least the value under § 8(3) sentence 1 EStG. Costs per recipient a year count only up to EUR 10,000; the excess is taxed normally. A single gift costing more than EUR 10,000 is excluded in full (§ 37b(1) sentence 3 EStG; BMF letter of 19 May 2015, Rn. 21). It does not apply to company cars, official meal values, staff discounts, items under § 40(2) or shares (§ 37b(2) sentence 2). The choice is made once for the business year, but separately for third parties and for own employees; for own employees the calendar year counts (BMF letter of 19 May 2015, BStBl I p. 468, Rn. 4). Items costing up to EUR 10 are treated as promotional giveaways and can be left out (same letter). The recipient is told the tax was paid and leaves the item out of income (§ 37b(3) EStG). For own employees the item stays subject to contributions: the third-party employee exclusion from social-insurance pay applies only where those employees are not employed by a company affiliated with the giver; affiliation does not itself establish a separate identical social assessment (§ 1(1) no. 14 SvEV).

de-payroll-benefits.before: - Staff events: if open to all staff, costs up to EUR 110 per event and attending employee are not pay, for up to two events a year. The cost is all the employer's costs including VAT, shared over the attendees, and the share of an employee's companions counts as the employee's (§ 19(1) no. 1a EStG). Only the excess is pay, which can be taxed at 25% (§ 40(2) sentence 1 no. 2 EStG).
de-payroll-benefits.after: - Staff events: if open to all staff of the business or a business unit, costs up to EUR 110 per event and attending employee are not pay, for up to two events a year. The cost is all the employer's costs including VAT, shared over the attendees, and the share of an employee's companions counts as the employee's (§ 19(1) no. 1a EStG). Only the excess is pay, which can be taxed at 25% (§ 40(2) sentence 1 no. 2 EStG).

de-payroll-benefits.before: - **§ 40(2), 25% and 15%.** Canteen meals, trip meals, staff events beyond the EUR 110 allowance, recreation grants within the limits, data-processing devices and internet subsidies, chargers and bikes given outright: 25%. Commuting subsidies and the car commute benefit, up to what the employee could claim as commuting costs: 15%. Public transport benefits can also be taxed at 25% instead of being tax-free, so the employee's commuting deduction is not reduced (§ 40(2) EStG). Items taxed under § 40(2) are free of contributions (§ 1(1) no. 3 SvEV).
de-payroll-benefits.after: - **§ 40(2), 25% and 15%.** Canteen meals, trip meals, staff events beyond the EUR 110 allowance, recreation grants within the limits, data-processing devices and internet subsidies, chargers and bikes given outright: 25%. Commuting subsidies and the car commute benefit, up to what the employee could claim as commuting costs: 15%. Public transport benefits can also be taxed at 25% instead of being tax-free, so the employee's commuting deduction is not reduced (§ 40(2) EStG). Items taxed under § 40(2) are free of contributions (§ 1(1) no. 3 SvEV). Apply the actual branch conditions: canteen meals must not be agreed wage components; for recreation grants, the employer must ensure recreational use and aggregate the earlier grants in the same year against the employee/spouse/child caps. Transfers of data-processing devices/accessories/internet access, internet-use subsidies, charger transfers/subsidies and outright transfers of non-motor bicycles require additionality to pay already owed. The 15% cash commuting subsidy also requires additionality, and amounts taxed under that 15% route reduce the employee's commuting deduction. The alternative 25% public-transport election instead covers all relevant § 3 no. 15 benefits of that calendar year uniformly, may apply without additionality, and does not reduce the commuting deduction. Staff-event allowance and the stated 25% route require access for all staff of the business or a business unit.

de-payroll-benefits.before: - **Low-earner subsidy (§ 100).** If the employee's current pay is not over EUR 2,575 a month (EUR 30,900 a year) when the contribution is made, and the employer pays at least EUR 240 a year on top of pay owed, the employer deducts 30% of that contribution, at most EUR 288, from the wage tax it pays over. The employer contribution under § 100 is tax-free up to EUR 960 a year, in addition to § 3 no. 63 (§ 100 EStG).
de-payroll-benefits.after: - **Low-earner subsidy (§ 100).** If the employee's current pay is not over EUR 2,575 a month (EUR 30,900 a year) when the contribution is made, and the employer pays at least EUR 240 a year on top of pay owed, the employer deducts 30% of that contribution, at most EUR 288, from the wage tax it pays over. The employer contribution under § 100 is tax-free up to EUR 960 a year, in addition to § 3 no. 63 (§ 100 EStG). This requires the first employment, an eligible Pensionsfonds/Pensionskasse/Direktversicherung with the payout arrangement required by § 82(2) sentence 2, German wage-tax treatment in the contribution period, and the same percentage distribution-cost charge on each contribution (a permitted recalculation cannot exceed the original percentage). Test the pay limit at the contribution date; later changes ordinarily do not alter entitlement. If this employer already made an additional contribution in 2016, cap the subsidy at the amount paid above that 2016 contribution: for qualifying current EUR 700 and 2016 EUR 600, min(EUR 210, EUR 288, EUR 100) gives EUR 100. If a funded entitlement later lapses and money returns to the employer, repay the subsidy to the extent attributable to that repayment by adding it to wage tax in the return for the receipt period (§ 100(1)–(4)).

de-payroll-benefits.before: - **Tax.** Employer contributions from the first employment to a Pensionsfonds, Pensionskasse or Direktversicherung are tax-free up to 8% of the pension ceiling: EUR 8,112 in 2026 (§ 3 no. 63 EStG; ceiling from SVBezGrV 2026). This includes amounts the employee converts from pay (Entgeltumwandlung).
de-payroll-benefits.after: - **Tax.** Employer contributions from the first employment to a Pensionsfonds, Pensionskasse or Direktversicherung are tax-free up to 8% of the pension ceiling: EUR 8,112 in 2026 (§ 3 no. 63 EStG; ceiling from SVBezGrV 2026). This includes amounts the employee converts from pay (Entgeltumwandlung). The promised pension/disability/survivor payout must meet § 82(2) sentence 2, and § 3 no. 63 does not apply to the extent the employee has made the § 1a(3) BetrAVG election for § 10a/section XI support. Separately conditioned termination contributions under sentence 3 have a tax ceiling of 4% of the pension ceiling × calendar years of employment with that employer, at most ten years. Qualifying catch-up contributions for years when the first employment was suspended and no German taxable wage was received from that employer have the sentence 4 ceiling of 8% × number of those years, at most ten. Two qualifying termination years therefore give EUR 8,112 under that route. Do not add distinct routes without checking their actual interaction; these special tax rules do not establish an extra social-insurance exemption.

de-payroll-benefits.before: - **Old contracts.** Unfunded Pensionskasse contributions are tax-free up to 4% of the ceiling, less § 3 no. 63 amounts (§ 3 no. 56 EStG), and can be flat-taxed at 20% up to EUR 1,752 a year (§ 40b EStG). Direktversicherung and Pensionskasse contracts where at least one contribution was flat-taxed under the pre-2005 § 40b before 1 January 2018 keep that 20% flat tax, and those amounts reduce the § 3 no. 63 limit (§ 52(4) sentence 23 and § 52(40) EStG).
de-payroll-benefits.after: - **Old contracts.** Unfunded Pensionskasse contributions are tax-free up to 4% of the ceiling, less amounts exempt under § 3 no. 63 sentences 1, 3 or 4 (§ 3 no. 56 EStG), and can be flat-taxed at 20% up to EUR 1,752 a year (§ 40b EStG). Direktversicherung and Pensionskasse contracts where at least one contribution was flat-taxed under the pre-2005 § 40b before 1 January 2018 keep that 20% flat tax, and those amounts reduce the § 3 no. 63 limit (§ 52(4) sentence 23 and § 52(40) EStG). The § 3 no. 56 route also requires first employment and the specified § 82(2) sentence 2 payout arrangement. For § 40b(2), EUR 1,752 is the ordinary individual first-employment limit: the pooled rule uses the average contribution per eligible worker, excluding workers with contributions above EUR 2,148. For contributions on termination, the EUR 1,752 limit is multiplied by calendar years with that employer, without the pooled rule, then reduced by the relevant § 40b(1) flat-taxed contributions in the termination year and six preceding years. These actual conditions qualify the ordinary annual shortcuts; the separate preserved pre-2005-contract gate remains.

de-payroll-benefits.before: - Employee shares in the employer's company up to EUR 2,000 a year if open to all staff with one year's service (§ 3 no. 39 EStG). For companies founded not more than 20 years ago and within twice the EU SME turnover and balance-sheet limits and four times the headcount limit (now or in any of the six previous years), the rest of the benefit can be deferred until sale, 15 years, or leaving the employer (§ 19a(1), (3), (4) EStG). The 15-year and leaving triggers do not apply if the employer declares irrevocably, by the next wage tax return, that it will be liable for the tax on a later sale (§ 19a(4a) EStG). Deferred share benefits are still subject to contributions (§ 1(1) no. 1 SvEV).
de-payroll-benefits.after: - Employee shares in the employer's company up to EUR 2,000 a year if open to all staff with one year's service (§ 3 no. 39 EStG). For § 19a deferral, the permitted employer-company holdings must be transferred free or below value in addition to pay already owed, and the employee must consent in payroll. Apply the actual incorporated § 19a(3) SME test: double the referenced Article 2(1) financial thresholds and four times its headcount threshold, determined under Articles 4 and 5 of that Recommendation, at transfer or in one of the six prior calendar years; formation must be no more than 20 years earlier. Do not replace that incorporated test with an unverified simple turnover/balance-sheet Boolean. For a qualifying group-company holding, aggregate the thresholds across all group companies and no group company may be older than 20 years. The deferred benefit becomes taxable on any whole or partial paid or unpaid transfer, including the specified § 17/§ 20 events or a contribution to business assets, or after 15 years, or on leaving the employer (§ 19a(1)–(4)). An irrevocable employer liability declaration made by the wage tax return following the relevant event postpones the 15-year/leaving triggers to that transfer event, not merely a sale (§ 19a(4a)). For a qualifying business-related decline, if actual fair value less the employee's original payment is below the deferred benefit, only that lower amount is taxed; on leaving and buyback by the employer, an employer shareholder or a group company, the paid consideration replaces fair value. The reduction does not apply to non-business-related declines or corporate measures such as distributions/capital repayments. With deferred benefit EUR 8,000, qualifying fair value EUR 5,000 and original employee payment EUR 1,000, taxable benefit is EUR 4,000. Deferred share benefits remain subject to contributions (§ 1(1) no. 1 SvEV); tax deferral alone is not contribution relief.

de-payroll-benefits.before: - **Social insurance.** Workers posted to or from Germany under an A1 certificate stay in their home system; benefits are then contribution-free in Germany. The status test for directors applies only where German social insurance law applies.
de-payroll-benefits.after: - **Social insurance.** An A1 certificate identifies which state's social-insurance law applies. While a valid binding certificate establishes another state's law, there are no additional German contributions on that basis. A German-law A1 for an outgoing posting instead documents continuation of German law: apply the German benefit valuation/contribution rules as applicable, rather than treating the benefit as contribution-free merely because there is an A1. The certificate binds until invalidated or withdrawn by the issuer ([DVKA applicable-law guidance](https://www.dvka.de/de/arbeitgeber-erwerbstaetige/faq/)). The status test for directors applies where German social-insurance law applies.

de-payroll-benefits.before: - **Effect.** If the decision is "self-employed", the director's pay is still wage income for wage tax, but no social insurance is due.
de-payroll-benefits.after: - **Effect.** If the decision is "self-employed", the director's pay remains wage income for wage tax, but that classification does not create employment-based social-insurance contributions. It is not a universal exemption from all social insurance: determine separate health cover, any compulsory self-employed pension category and other status-specific duties under [de-social-contributions](de-social-contributions.md). No particular director's alternative duty is assumed solely from this classification.

de-payroll-benefits.before: - **Managing directors.** If a director treated as self-employed is later found employed, contributions are due for the whole period, subject to limitation; the status procedure is the protection against this (§ 7a SGB IV). The July 2026 BSG case shows the size: EUR 127,833.77 in contributions and levies claimed after an audit.
de-payroll-benefits.after: - **Managing directors.** If a director treated as self-employed is later found employed, ordinary contributions can reach the whole period, subject to limitation, unless the actual individual § 7a(5) or qualifying group-opinion § 7a(4c) protection applies as explained in de-social-contributions; the procedures are not automatic protection. Retrospective late-payment surcharges are separately excluded to the extent credible no-fault lack of knowledge is shown under § 24(2) SGB IV (§ 7a SGB IV). The July 2026 BSG case shows the size: EUR 127,833.77 in contributions and levies claimed after an audit.
